purpose: Test stable-identity routing under arbitrary slot permutations and variable pool sizes, while learning add/remove/retype/strength topology changes from task loss.

task.name: permuted_keyed_memory
task.slot_permutation: Each example independently places valid stable identities in random slots among padded positions; the readout slot also varies.
task.initial_topology: Two persistent edges per sample: one query edge with a randomized relation type and strength, plus one distractor edge. No edge/action labels are supplied to the task optimizer.
task.targets: Single-link task routes 0.60 times the queried value. Two-link task routes 0.60 times the queried value plus 0.35 times its cyclic successor. Correct topology requires add, remove, retype, and strength update actions across examples.

model.candidate_set: all valid memory-identity to readout-identity links

training.topology_gradient: straight-through hard-action forward with softmax task-loss gradient; no edge/action labels

controls.parameter_matched: stable-identity-canonicalized flat MLP with nearest integer hidden width to graph model parameter count
controls.linear_mac_matched: stable-identity-canonicalized flat MLP with nearest integer hidden width to graph model per-example linear MAC count
controls.linear_mac_contract: Counts Linear output elements times input width for batch size one; scatter, reductions, pointwise ops, optimizer and memory traffic are excluded. Wall time is separately measured.
controls.identity_canonicalization: Scatter valid neurons into stable identity-indexed slots; padding contributes zeros, so comparisons do not penalize controls for arbitrary slot permutations.

decision_rules.quality_ci: Paired per-seed relative MSE delta; 95% two-sided t interval upper bound must be below zero.
decision_rules.interpretation: Thresholds are fixed before the run; unmet results stay unmet and are not tuned after observing test data.

limitations: Synthetic retrieval/composition tasks do not establish natural-language or broad capability claims.
The stable identity registry is caller-owned; this experiment varies node slots and uses remap_node_ids tests, but does not serialize registries across process restarts.
Linear MAC is a transparent proxy rather than total FLOPs; empirical MPS step time is the end-to-end cost measure.
MPS and host memory use 2 ms sampling and can miss shorter peaks.
Pool-size generalization is tested only over 4 to 16 memory neurons in this run.
